title: Schematic image of a partial section of a separated algebraic-space morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:B\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $f$ is separated, meaning that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $a:O\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] which is quasi-compact: its pullback to every affine scheme over $Y$ has quasi-compact source. Let $s:O\to B$ satisfy $fs=a$. Then there exist a closed subspace $i:C\hookrightarrow B$ and $t:O\to C$ with $it=s$, such that $C$ is the smallest closed subspace of $B$ through which $s$ factors. Moreover the morphism $C\times_YO\to O$ induced by $fi$ is an isomorphism, and under this isomorphism the map $O\to C\times_YO$ induced by $t$ and $\mathrm{id}_O$ is its inverse. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No Noetherian, finite-type, reducedness, or properness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CP3, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-of-partial-section; existence and smallest-closed-subspace property: Tag 082X, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image; restriction used in its proof: Tag 082Z, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image.

proof.text: The diagonal of $f$ is quasi-compact: after any affine scheme test it is a closed immersion, whose source is a closed subset of a quasi-compact affine spectrum, hence quasi-compact. Thus $f$ is quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qc-cancellation] to $O\xrightarrow{s}B\xrightarrow{f}Y$; its composite is the given quasi-compact $a$, so $s$ is quasi-compact. That node's quasi-compactness says that $|O\times_BT|$ is quasi-compact for every affine scheme $T\to B$; by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] each such $O\times_BT$ then has a representable surjective etale map from an affine, hence quasi-compact, scheme, which is the quasi-compactness of $s$ required by the pushforward theorem of Step 2. Also $s$ is a monomorphism: $su=sv$ implies $au=av$, hence $u=v$ since an open immersion is a subfunctor inclusion. Consequently $\Delta_s:O\to O\times_BO$ is an isomorphism and is a closed immersion on scheme tests. Thus $s$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 0CP3, proof, first sentence; Tag 03KS, lemma-quasi-compact-permanence; separated implies quasi-separated by the scheme-test definition.

proof.text: The structure modules $\mathcal O_O$ and $\mathcal O_B$ are quasi-coherent: each has the presentation $0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal O\to0$. By the quasi-compact separated pushforward theorem and Step 1, $s_*\mathcal O_O$ is quasi-coherent. Hence the kernel theorem makes $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_B\to s_*\mathcal O_O)$ quasi-coherent; it is an ideal because the displayed map is a ring map. The ideal/closed-subspace correspondence gives $i:C=V(\mathcal I)\hookrightarrow B$. Since $\mathcal I\to s_*\mathcal O_O$ is zero, its factorization criterion gives $t:O\to C$ with $it=s$.

source.place: Tags 082X, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image, and 082Z, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, construction of the kernel ideal; Tag 03M9, lemma-pushforward. Kernel closure is spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1, lemma-properties-quasi-coherent (3).

proof.text: Let $D\hookrightarrow B$ be a closed subspace through which $s$ factors, and let $\mathcal J$ be its corresponding quasi-coherent ideal. The factorization criterion says that $\mathcal J\to s_*\mathcal O_O$ is zero; hence $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$. The inclusion-reversing bijection gives $C=V(\mathcal I)\subseteq V(\mathcal J)=D$. Thus $C$ has the required smallest-closed-subspace property.

source.place: Tag 082X, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image; Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals, inclusion-reversing bijection and factorization criterion.

proof.text: Put $B_O=B\times_YO$, write $q:B_O\to B$ and $p:B_O\to O$ for its projections, and let $g=(s,\mathrm{id}_O):O\to B_O$. The square with top map $g$, bottom map $B\to B\times_YB$ equal to $\Delta_f$, left map $s:O\to B$, and right map $h:B_O\to B\times_YB$, $h(b,o)=(b,s(o))$, is cartesian: its test sections are exactly the pairs $(b,o)$ with $b=s(o)$. Therefore $g$ is a closed immersion. Indeed on each scheme test it is a scheme base change of a test of $\Delta_f$, and a quotient $A\to A/J$ remains a surjective quotient after any ring base change. Also $q$ is an open immersion, directly by the scheme-test definition applied to the base change of $a$. Finally $O\times_BB_O\simeq O$ over $B_O$, with map $g$: its test sections have $a(o_1)=a(o_2)$, so $o_1=o_2$.

source.place: Tag 0CP3, proof, section over the open; Tag 03KP, lemma-section-immersion (3), here written out as the pullback of the diagonal.

proof.text: Restrict the ring map defining $\mathcal I$ to the open subspace $B_O$. The direct-image restriction comparison identifies it with $\mathcal O_{B_O}\to g_*\mathcal O_O$: on a scheme chart $T\to B_O$ both direct images are compatible sections over $O\times_BT=O\times_{B_O}T$, using the identification in Step 4, and the ring maps send a section to its same pullback. Restriction to an open is restriction to the full subsite of charts mapping into that open, so it preserves the sectionwise kernel. Thus $\mathcal I|_{B_O}=\ker(\mathcal O_{B_O}\to g_*\mathcal O_O)$. By the ideal correspondence and its base-change formula, the left side defines $C\times_BB_O$ (on an open, the pulled-back ideal is its restriction), and the right side defines the closed subspace $g:O\hookrightarrow B_O$ from Step 4. The bijection therefore identifies these two closed subspaces over $B_O$.

source.place: Tag 03LX, lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules, degree-zero comparison and its section formula, applied to the open restriction; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 082Z (3) and 03MB with the inverse-image paragraph.

proof.text: Associate the fibre products to obtain $C\times_BB_O\simeq C\times_YO$. The identification of Step 5 is induced by $(t,\mathrm{id}_O):O\to C\times_YO$, since after mapping to $B_O$ it is $g=(s,\mathrm{id}_O)$ and the closed inclusion is a monomorphism. Its composite with the projection $r:C\times_YO\to O$ is the identity. Since it is an isomorphism, this equality makes $r$ its inverse; in particular $r$ is an isomorphism and its inverse is exactly the map required in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem partialSection_schematicImage {S : Scheme.{u}} (B Y O : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : B ⟶ Y) (hsep : IsSeparatedPresheafMap f.hom.hom) (a : O ⟶ Y) (hopen : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) a.hom.hom) (hqc : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ QuasiCompact p.left) a.hom.hom) (s : O ⟶ B) (hs : s ≫ f = a) : ∃ (C : ClosedSubspace B) (t : O ⟶ (C.val : AlgebraicSpace S)), t ≫ C.val.arrow = s ∧ (∀ D : ClosedSubspace B, (∃ v : O ⟶ (D.val : AlgebraicSpace S), v ≫ D.val.arrow = s) → C.val ≤ D.val) ∧ ∃ e : Limits.pullback (C.val.arrow ≫ f).hom a.hom ≅ O.obj, e.hom = Limits.pullback.snd (C.val.arrow ≫ f).hom a.hom ∧ e.inv ≫ Limits.pullback.fst (C.val.arrow ≫ f).hom a.hom = t.hom
lean.note: Uses the existing ClosedSubspace and IsSeparatedPresheafMap definitions, whose landed definition nodes are added to stmt_deps. For the representable open immersion a, scheme-test quasi-compactness is expressed with the existing Mathlib QuasiCompact predicate. The sheaf-pullback isomorphism has forward map the second projection; its inverse has first component t, and its second component is the identity by the inverse law. The accepted natural-language statement and proof are unchanged.
